headline: No documented pairwise interaction; both open-source agents show no network egress and no shared I/O surfaces, so prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict pathways are not evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile exposes shared communication channels, I/O surfaces, or runnable integration points. agent_a has no I/O surfaces and agent_b likewise has none, so there is no documented path for one to inject instructions into the other by default.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected through a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep both agents isolated from shared folders and clipboards.
Do not add an MCP or message-queue bridge without provenance checks.
Review any future connector for instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents are documented with network_egress:none and empty data_classes_touched, so there is no evidenced route for sensitive data to flow between them or out to a third party in the current profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is configured to read shared files containing sensitive data, leakage risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared workspace.
Recheck data-class handling before enabling any upload connector.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surfaces, OAuth scopes, git access, or concurrency primitives are documented for either agent. With empty io_surfaces and empty concurrency_model fields, a write-write conflict pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repository, conflict risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disabled unless needed.
Add locking before enabling shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The profiles do not show either agent producing authoritative outputs that the other consumes, and both are unverified docs-only entries with no runnable integration. Without a documented handoff, cascading error is not evidenced.
conditions: IF one agent's output is wired directly into the other's prompt or action step, cascading error risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require structured validation of any handoff.
Log and diff outputs before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles show empty data_classes_touched. The compliance-mismatch pathway is therefore not evidenced in this pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance review becomes necessary.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data until policies are confirmed.
Document retention and residency settings if added later.
